findings.basis: The source is one file: Motorola's carrier config as imported into LineageOS's android_device_motorola_lyriq (commit title names stock build V1TLS35.73-60-3-14). 2026-10-24 is the import date; the value's own age is not known, and stock itself was not read. Each listed block states the value explicitly for its exact network code and GID. Blocks 639, 644, 754, 755, 756, 761. Identity: Samsung's 2026-08 and 2026-09 rules list gid1 8030 and 9030 on 302-220 and 313-340 as Dish 5G, gid1 6532 on 313-340 as Dish 5G and gid1 6730 on 313-340 as Dish 5G Data only. Samsung's IMS data also carries gid1 8030 and 9030 with gid2 values as Dish US on 302-220, so these are GIDs of real Dish SIMs. The value: Google's dish5gsa_us sets allow_hold_call_during_emergency_bool false, rtt_supported_bool true and rtt_supported_while_roaming_bool true for every Dish GID it lists on 313-340 and for Dish's IMSI ranges; the same three values stand in each Motorola block here. Google's lane has no rule for these GIDs, so 'unset' here means Google does not list them, not that it states another value. These blocks are not marked: their code text reads back unchanged, so the LineageOS build applied them. Read cbb4ccfd78f3 already passes true for the plain 313-340 profile.
findings.effect: rtt_supported_while_roaming_bool (CarrierConfigManager.java:10991-10992, default false at :12197) only narrows RTT while roaming, and every reader sits behind rtt_supported_bool: ImsRegistrationTracker.isRttSupported reads it only once RTT provisioning is on (ImsRegistrationTracker.java:585-598), which needs rtt_supported_bool (ImsManager.java:2756-2797); AosCondition.IsRttSupported returns false first when rtt_supported_bool is false (AosCondition.cpp:998-1011); TelecomAccountRegistry needs isRttEnabled, which is false while config_support_rtt is false (TelecomAccountRegistry.java:1136-1154, PhoneInterfaceManager.java:7995-8035, config.xml:235, same on lineage-24.0). The emergency registration does not read it (AosHandleEmergencyMtc.cpp:45-63). Emergency routing and TTY routing do not read it (EmergencyCallDomainSelector.java:755-756, 2045-2057). With RTT on, true lets the roaming registration carry TEXT and stops the native TTY-mode deregistration while roaming (AosCondition.cpp:1026-1031). On a phone: admitted only for the most specific profile that sets the key, else the Google-lane value, else Android's default false (Serving.kt:405-440).
findings.risk: Only with rtt_supported_bool true, which the read of that key passes for these six profiles: the roaming registration carries TEXT, and the network can refuse it (AosRegistration.cpp:1210-1245). The emergency registration and emergency and TTY routing do not read this key. No priority path reads it.

notes: Proceed. The key only extends the normal-registration RTT capability to roaming, and the value is Google's for the same operator.
